en.title: Lanterns Composer Reveals the Sad, Badass Heart of John Stewart's Theme
en.summary: Discover how composer Stephanie Economou crafted the iconic theme for John Stewart in HBO's Lanterns, balancing the character's profound loneliness with his undeniable strength. The music reflects a complex hero finding his voice.
en.body:
The latest episode of **Lanterns** gave us a deeper look into the origins of **John Stewart**, portrayed by **Aaron Pierre**. It's a character-driven series, and composer **Stephanie Economou** made sure **Stewart's** theme resonated with his intricate personality. Economou shared that she began by strumming simple chords that immediately felt like **John** himself. "They were quite lonely. They were steady and confident, but sad in a way. There was a sadness to it," she explained. Yet, this wasn't the whole story of the character. "But he’s also pretty badass, so I wanted to write him a riff that encapsulated that as well." The result is a musical motif that perfectly captures the duality of a hero who carries a heavy past but possesses an unyielding spirit.

Economou’s approach to scoring **John Stewart**’s theme involved finding that delicate balance. The music needed to convey the weight of his experiences while also highlighting his inherent power and resilience. This careful composition ensures that the audience feels the character’s internal struggle and his emerging heroism simultaneously. It’s a testament to Economou’s skill that a single musical theme can so effectively communicate such complex emotional layers, making **John Stewart** an even more compelling figure within the **Lanterns** narrative.

## Scoring the Spectrum of Emotion

Beyond **John Stewart's** theme, Economou discussed her broader approach to the series' score. She touched upon how external musical elements, like pre-existing songs used in specific scenes, might influence her original compositions. The interview revealed that while these "needle drops" can set a mood, they don't dictate the direction of her score. Instead, Economou focuses on building themes that evolve alongside the characters throughout the season. This suggests that the musical landscape of **Lanterns** is as dynamic as its plot, with themes for characters like **Hal Jordan** (Kyle Chandler) also undergoing significant shifts as their stories progress.

## Fan Connection Through Sound

For the dedicated fanbase of **Lanterns**, understanding the composer's intent behind **John Stewart's** theme adds a rich layer to their viewing experience. The revelation that the music directly mirrors the character's blend of melancholy and strength offers a new lens through which to appreciate **Aaron Pierre's** performance. It’s this kind of insight into the craft behind the screen that passionate fans crave, deepening their connection to the characters and the world of **Lanterns**. Economou's work ensures that even the quieter, more introspective moments are underscored with a power that speaks volumes about the hero's journey.

## What's Next

Fans eager to hear more of **Stephanie Economou's** evolving score for **Lanterns** can anticipate further thematic developments as the season unfolds. The composer has indicated that character themes will continue to adapt, promising a rich and dynamic auditory experience alongside the unfolding narrative.

When you first got the project for Lanterns , what was your process for coming together with the theme overall, and specifically for the two main characters, John and Hal. My first port of call was to start writing some theme suites away from picture, just to gauge [showrunner] Chris Mundy’s reaction to questions like: Do you feel like this is the right sound world? Do you feel like this tune speaks more profoundly to the Green Lanterns? I believe the first thing I wrote was the Lanterns theme. I wrote a two or three minute suite of that tune on piano and GuitarViols, and strings, and synths, just to get his reaction. And he listened to it and he said, “Yep, this is it.” And I felt like I would be able to put that theme through its paces—it can get intimate at moments. It can get really grand. It could be quite unsettling and unstable in other moments. So I did that one, and then I wrote a suite of what became the alien theme because I was really excited from the scripts to explore what that world would be like.
